newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MARK, DOLLAR ACTIVE ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MKT.
newsitem.headline: MARK, DOLLAR ACTIVE ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MKT.

text.p: Hungary's foreign currency futures markets saw moderate turnover dominated by basket deals in the mark and dollar, dealers said.

Total turnover of foreign currency futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) was 2.09 billion forints, up from Wednesday's tiny 780 million, while the much smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw relatively high volume of almost 890 million forints.
On the BCE the mark and dollar were in focus with half of all turnover in basket deals involving both currencies.

Basket deals are seen as a means of hedging against future large fluctuations of the dollar/mark and are based on the central bank's currency basket against which the forint is devalued by 1.1 percent per month.
The basket is made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.

The September mark fell 0.14 to 112.01 forints, while dollar futures for the same month were steady at 191.40. The other popular month for basket deals was March, with the mark steady at 118.80 and the dollar up 0.30 to 201.80.
Significant interest remained for deferred maturities in both the yen and the Swiss franc, whose low interest rates dealers believe make them a good long-term hedge against the devaluing forint.
The March yen saw a quarter of all BCE trade, falling 0.25 to 167.01, while the December Swiss franc also saw significant turnover and fell 0.17 to 137.51.

Trade on the BSE, which deals only in the mark, dollar and Ecu, centred around shorter term deals in the mark and dollar, including a large basket deal for May, which traders said reflected current fluctuations of the spot dollar/mark.

"The market has come to life in the last two days," said Attila Gazdik of New York Broker. "There's strong demand from buyers and sellers as they see an opportunity to hedge on the changing prices (of the mark and the dollar)."

The central bank quoted the four currencies in its midday fix at 104.91 forints to the mark, up 0.10, 181.21 for the dollar, up 0.44, 123.35 for the Swiss franc, dowm 0.02, and 144.15 per 100 yen, up 0.72.
